mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months indicates an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with declining FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC between FEDFUNDS trend and SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases corporate borrowing costs and reduces earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC between FEDFUNDS threshold and SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (PAYEMS > 159000) combined with weak consumer spending (RSAFS < 730000) signals overheating inflationary pressures that trigger Fed rate hikes, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting PAYEMS > 159000 AND RSAFS < 730000, or Rank IC between interaction signal and SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High consumer spending (RSAFS > 750000) during expansionary phases indicates robust corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with RSAFS > 750000, or Rank IC between RSAFS and SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.5%) indicates tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with declining UNRATE, or Rank IC between UNRATE trend and SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rises above 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals economic contraction that reduces corporate earnings visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with UNRATE > 5.0% for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC between UNRATE threshold and SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) combined with rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 3.5%) signals economic weakness and policy tightening, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting INDPRO < 100 AND FEDFUNDS > 3.5%, or Rank IC between interaction signal and SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production growth (INDPRO > 102) during expansionary phases indicates robust corporate output and earnings momentum, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with INDPRO > 102, or Rank IC between INDPRO and SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
